problems.statement: The 98.1% on-time figure is a metric artifact: the bonus (effective Mar 2026, Pell Jul 2026) rewards the on-time % while dispatchers can freely overwrite the Promised Delivery Date, so revisions are used to protect the number and the KPI no longer measures service against the customer's original promise.
RouteWise caused the on-time improvement (CEO's explanation).
Revisions reflect legitimate customer requests and weather (Northgate manager's explanation).
Real service has not improved and has probably worsened: customer-measured on-time fell, lateness complaints rose, and the largest customer is moving 30% of lanes to tender.
The rise in lateness complaints is only a portal artifact (customer service manager's explanation).

A driver shortage on mountain lanes is a real underlying capacity problem generating late freight and many of the Operational-Capacity revisions, but it does not explain the sudden network-wide step change in revisions.

Governance and control gap: revisions are unaudited, notification to the customer is optional, supervisors reinforce number protection, and few dispatchers escalate concerns, so no one monitors the original-date on-time rate and leadership relies on the manipulated KPI.
Launching the 98 out of 100 advertising campaign would create misleading-claim, reputational and customer-trust risk.
Raising the top bonus tier to 99% would intensify the incentive to revise dates and further decouple the metric from service.

causalClaims.from: Dispatcher on-time bonus tied to the revisable TMS KPI
causalClaims.to: Surge in promised-date revisions (about 5x) and late entries with Operational-Capacity reason
Reported on-time rising from about 91% to about 98%
Customer-experienced lateness, lower Brightwell on-time and tender threat

actions.action: Halt or postpone the 12 January '98 out of 100, on time' campaign until the claim is re-based on original promised dates and verified.
actions.rationale: The claim is unsupported by customer-measured data and risks misleading-advertising exposure and reputational damage when customers know otherwise.

actions.action: Freeze the proposed raise of the top bonus tier to 99% ($1,500).
actions.rationale: It would amplify the incentive that is already driving revision gaming and cost more for no real service gain.

actions.action: Recompute on-time for Mar-Sep 2026 and prior periods against the original promised date from the revision log, by center, lane and reason code.
actions.rationale: This is the cheapest verification of the probable cause and gives the true service baseline.

actions.action: Redesign the dispatcher incentive and KPI: measure against original or customer-confirmed dates, add audit and approval for late or Operational-Capacity revisions, and make customer notification mandatory.
actions.rationale: Removes the structural mismatch between reward and real service while keeping honest ETA updates.

actions.action: Contact Brightwell and other large accounts with a transparent recovery plan before the Q1 tender review.
actions.rationale: Protects the largest revenue relationship, which is already signalling departure over unreported date changes.

actions.action: Address the driver shortage on the mountain lanes (recruitment, retention, relay planning) as a separate capacity workstream.
actions.rationale: It is a real contributor to lateness, but it does not explain the revision spike and fixing it will not repair the KPI.

actions.action: Retroactively claw back bonuses or discipline dispatchers.
actions.rationale: The incentive and permissions were designed by management, and punishing staff would suppress honest reporting and the escalation the organization needs.

actions.action: Credit RouteWise with on-time gains and roll it out on that basis.
actions.rationale: Its documented benefits are miles and fuel only, and on-time rose before Northgate had it.

actions.action: Run the campaign with a softened or footnoted claim without re-basing the metric.
actions.rationale: The figure remains misleading and still exposes the firm to customer and regulatory backlash.

actions.action: Dismiss the complaint rise as a portal artifact.
actions.rationale: The increase is confined to lateness complaints and is consistent with Brightwell's logs.

nextEvidence: On-time rate recomputed against the original promised date from the revision log, by dispatch center, lane, month and reason code, compared with the 98.1% reported.
Audit sample of late-entered Operational-Capacity revisions: actual delivery date vs original date, whether the customer was notified, and supervisor instructions.
Delivery performance against customer-booked dates for other large accounts (like Brightwell's receiving logs) and complaint categories by channel to separate portal effects from service.
output.summary: The 98.1% on-time figure is mainly an artifact of incentive plus metric design. Dispatchers can overwrite the promised date, and the bonus rewards the resulting percentage. Revisions rose about 5x in each center right after its bonus eligibility, with late, capacity-coded and un-notified entries, while RouteWise, weather and customer requests do not explain the step. Brightwell's own logs show 81% on time against 87% a year ago, lateness complaints are up 35%, and 30% of its lanes face tender. Pause the campaign and the 99% bonus tier, recompute on-time against original dates, redesign the KPI and its controls, and engage key accounts. Treat the driver shortage as a separate, real problem.
